producer_report.summary:
In `hard` planning mode, an easy job is now planned when a Behavior criterion asks for a failing run without the fix. Root cause: the gate in `Athena::dispatch` looked only at `hard_reason`, so such a job got no plan. Athena then never ran its fails-without demonstration, and the verifier could not see it.

**Gate.** It is now `p.plans(reading.hard_reason.is_some() || asks_for_fails_without_run(&reading))`. The documented helper lowercases the criterion text and splits it on non-alphanumerics. It needs a word starting `fail` plus one of: `without the fix|change|mechanism|patch`, `without it`, `before the fix`, `on the base`, or `without` right after the fail word. Content criteria and a bare 'never fails' do not match. The helper reads only the reading, so `JobPlanConfig::plans(bool)` and its tests are unchanged. A doc-comment-only update went into config.rs.

**Test seam.** The core demo seam was cfg(test) only. I compiled `Guard` and `install` under `any(test, feature = "test-support")` and re-exported them as `athena_core::run::install_demo_runner` and `DemoRunnerGuard`. This lets the CLI test make the demonstration run a fake `sh -c` and see a real `fails-without-1` record. Production builds are unchanged.

**Tests.**
- A core unit test pins the wordings.
- A core hard-mode test checks the planned job and its `fails-without-1` record in the verifier prompt.
- A core hard-mode test checks that three non-matching criteria are not planned.
- A CLI test checks the planned job, the plan and critique records at HEAD and the `fails-without-1` record in the verifier prompt.

With the original gate restored, both planned-job tests failed with roles [Reader, Producer, Verifier]. I then put the new gate back. The verifier can see the same thing from the diff (the removed line) and by running the tests.

This fixes the earlier major finding. Criterion 3 now rests on the CLI test the verifier runs itself, not on an unrecorded command.

**Docs.** job-planning.md and CHANGELOG.md (Fixed, under [Unreleased]) state the rule and the root cause.

criteria_check.evidence: The gate is now `p.plans(reading.hard_reason.is_some() || asks_for_fails_without_run(&reading))`. The text is lowercased and split on non-alphanumerics, and it needs a `fail*` word plus an anchor phrase. The unit test `the_fails_without_helper_matches_singular_and_plural_wordings` covers 'tests fail without the change', 'a test fails without the fix', quoted forms and negatives. The diff shows the old line as the removed one, and running with it restored fails the planned-job tests.

The match is on free text, so a wording outside the anchor list (for example 'errors out without the change') is not planned. The structured fails_without field on the reading's Criterion stays out of scope.
The criterion 2 CLI test is the existing, unchanged `with_athena_toml_planning_hard_jobs_only_...` null-hard_reason case. The new not-planned assertions are in the core test.
mistakes: My first draft of the core test helper had a nonsensical hard_reason assertion (a no-op json expression). I replaced it with a plain null-or-absent check before running anything.
I kept the helper as two functions (one takes the reading, one takes the text) rather than the single function in the plan. The gate calls the reading-level one, and both have doc comments.
learnings: The core demo seam (`checks::demo_seam`) was cfg(test) only. A `test-support` build has no mapper, so it records no demonstration. The seam is now compiled under `any(test, feature = "test-support")` and re-exported as `athena_core::run::install_demo_runner` and `DemoRunnerGuard`.
The build enables rustc's missing-debug-implementations warning, so the newly widened `Guard` needed `#[derive(Debug)]`.

The producer prompt-visible criterion text must match across the reader, producer criteria_check and verifier criteria in the scripted core tests. A behavior criterion also needs a cited command, so the test wrapper sets verifier commands and `commands_run`.
Plain `grep` is blocked by the Bash hook; use the Grep tool.
desires: A way to run the revert check (original gate against the new tests) as an Athena-recorded step, so the verifier can see it instead of the producer reporting it.
